properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: LEATHERWOOD LLC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 12/15/2023
Violation Code: OGA3220(B) - PLUGGING REQUIREMENTS - Failure to notify DEP, the coal operator, lessee and owner prior to plugging a well underlain by coal and submit a plat.
Violation ID: 8168383
Permit API: 059-24992
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Morris Township
Inspection Type: Plugging(Includes Plugged/Mined Through)
Inspection Date: 12/15/2023
Comments: OGI staff Geoffrey Lutty and Justin Najewicz performed an onsite inspection of the Hopkins pad 059-24992. Plugging operations were ongoing but no crew was present onsite and activities were paused. The rig was hooked up to 059-24992. What appeared to be a small amount of oily substance was seen leaking from a line as seen in the attached photos. It is recommended to clean up the spill. What appeared to be brine was noted on the surface surrounding the wellhead. WQS follow up is being requested to evaluate if a brine release has occurred. No issues were noted with the well head, rig, tanks or associated equipment. Plugging operations did not commence within 30 days of submission of the NOI as required by 3220(b). A violation of 3220(b) has occurred. A new NOI was submitted for the well on 12/14/23 at 16:20. According to a December 13, 2023 email from Kevin Wright, Manager of Gas Well Plugging for Consol Energy, on 12/5/23 10k rated cast iron bridge plugs were set at 7,860 (7724 TVD) and 7824 (7711 TVD). At the time the plugs were set, an alternative method had not been approved for the well. The requested alternate method was not approved until 12/13/23. Violations of 78a75 and 3221 have occurred. Due to technical difficulties, these violations could not be added via inspection but will be issued under this inspection record in eFACTS.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/24/2024
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8202222
Permit API: 015-23909
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Herrick Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/24/2024
Comments: On 09/24/2024 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow up inspection of Chesapeake Appalachia's Hillis Location Well Pad in Herrick Township, Bradford County. The weather was 58 degrees and cloudy. I arrived 1100 hours. Rain fell on the pad within the last 24 hours. On 09/19/2024 the DEP received Chesapeake Appalachia's 15 day interim report in response to violations identified in Inspection Record No. 3826844 from 09/09/2024 and 380793 on 08/06/2024. This report was uploaded to eFACTS and it is attached as a document in this inspection report. The site appears stabilized with greater than 70% perennial vegetative cover. There was no accelerated erosion or sedimentation observed. The Post-Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) Best Management Practices (BMP's) remain in place and appear to be functioning properly. Pooled water on the pad during the time of inspection was field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 320-821 us/cm. There was no evidence of any spills or releases today. There are five wells capable of producing onsite. They are properly tagged with the American Petroleum Institute (API) identification numbers. Residual waste from surface scraping is being stored onsite it is on containment and it is covered (photo #3). This case has been referred to the Environmental cleanups and Brownfields program and all violations will remain outstanding until results have been reviewed and compared to Act 2 standards by the ECB program, and an approval letter has been issued. 35 P.S. 6018. 301 SWMA25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)CSL 402(b)I departed at 1200 hours.

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-12-27
Comments: This inspection is being conducted as a routine inspection of wells in the general area. WQS Eric Norman is assisting. Conditions on site are cloudy in the mid 50's. The Access road appears to be constructed with no accelerated erosion or sedimentation observed. The site appears constructed and in production with one Production Tank on site. The Production Tank is within an earthen dike which appears to be in good condition. No dead, dying, or distressed vegetation is observed. The well is labeled and appears to be in good condition. The Production Tank appears to have corrosion forming on the bottom three feet of the tank. No holes observed during this inspection. The Department recommends that the operator take immediate action to prevent further corrosion from occurring in order to prevent breaches from occurring in the primary containment. It appears that an animal may have dug a hole under the Production Tank. The Department recommends that the operator abate this in order to prevent structural integrity issues from arising. The Department is requesting Production Tank inspection reports from 10/01/2019 to 12/30/2019 for this site. The Department is issuing violations based on observations made during this inspection. Additional violations may be forthcoming based on information provided in the NOV response.

Report Details

Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 922941

Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/12/2021
Comments: The DEP conducted an incident inspection of JKLM's Headwaters 145 Pad located in Ulysses Township, Potter County on 7/12/2021 at 1040 hours. The weather was 76 degrees with mostly cloudy skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a reported release of ~42 gallons of production fluid to the pad surface. The release occurred on Saturday, 7/10/2021, and was properly reported to the DEP. Complaint ID #357917 is tied to this release. On 7/10/2021, at approximately 1210 hours, a fitting on a hose line connected to a production line riser failed, causing a reported release of ~42 gallons of production fluid to the pad surface. A vacuum truck was onsite when the release occurred and was able to vacuum up the fluid that was visible. Excavation of the pad material began on Saturday. A rain event on Sunday evening caused pooling of water in the excavated areas, which was again vacuumed up. Environmental consultant, Whipper Hill was onsite during the inspection on Monday, where screening and excavating of the impacted area was being conducted. Whipper Hill reported elevated soil conductivity readings from 3-6mS/cm. I screened the impacted area for soil conductivity with a Hanna Groline soil tester. Some isolated areas were field measured >4.00mS/cm. Standing water along the edge of the pad closest to the release was field measured at ~370us/cm today (see photo #5). The release was contained to the pad surface and no erosion & sediment controls or stormwater controls were affected. The impacted area was still being screened and excavated when I left the site. Based on the findings outlined within this inspection report, violations of the following are cited against API # 105-21875 at this time: 35 P.S. 691.402(b) 25 Pa. Code 78a.57(a) 35 P.S. 6018.301 Due to the volume of the release being reported at ~42 gallons and then a commingling of impacted soils and rainwater after the initial release, this release will be referred to the DEP's Cleanups and Brownfields Program for attainment with Act 2 standards. I departed the site at 1150 hours.

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 950242
Permit API: 117-22116
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/05/2022
Comments: The DEP conducted an incident inspection of Repsol's Johnson K 02-135 well site located in Hamilton Township, Tioga County on 4/5/2022 at 1030 hours. The weather was 54 degrees with mostly clear skies. This inspection was conducted in response to a reported release of produced water off containment. DEP Environmental Trainee, Brooke Millisock, assisted me during the inspection. ID #363183 is tied to this release within CTS. We spoke with Billy Watts (Repsol) and Ralph Babcock (Repsol) while onsite. On 4/4/2022 at approximately 1350 hours, a release of ~1 barrel of produced water to the pad surface and down the fill slope was discovered after pumping produced water from the offload tank area to the tank storage area. The release occurred due to a punctured hole in the produced water flowline. Upon discovery, flow was stopped and the pipe was wrapped with absorbents and tape to prevent additional produced water from releasing. The release was promptly reported to the DEP. Resource Environmental was dispatched to screen the impacted area and excavation was started. A third roll-off container was being utilized during today's inspection to dispose of impacted material. While onsite, the DEP screened areas within and around the excavated area. The majority of the release appears to have been cleaned up, however, a few areas were still found to be elevated in electrical conductivity. Some areas just outside of the initial excavated area were field measured at >4.00mS/cm, utilizing a Hanna GroLine soil conductivity meter. A small area near the top of the excavated area/fill slope was also field measured at >4.00mS/cm. Repsol plans to continue excavating impacted soil from the area. Based on the findings of today's inspection and based on the reported release of ~1 barrel of produced water off containment, the following violations are cited against API #117-22116 at this time: 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a) 35 P.S. 6018.301 35 P.S. 691.402(b) Upon attainment with Act 2 Standards, the violations will then be closed out. We departed the site at 1145 hours.

Comments: This well was drilled in a forested area off of Point View Road in March 2006. Since the most recent inspection of the site on 8/30/2021 (Inspection Record # 3242810), work has been started on remediation of the site. A spill was reported to the Department on 11:03 AM on August 27, 2021. The spill occurred from a broken copper line attached to the wellhead. The estimated volume lost from this spill was 2 bbl. During this inspection, it was noted that the production equipment has been disconnected and staged along the edge of the restored site. Stressed vegetation and contaminated soil has been removed from the site. A response to the NOV has been received by the Department. The response states that five tri-axle loads of contaminated soil and vegetation were removed from the site. The response also states that the excavation will be left open until the attainment of standards from the Alternative Remediation Process has been demonstrated. The violations at the site can be closed when the contaminated soil has been replaced, the site has been graded to final contours, and the manifest and tipping information for soil disposal has been received by the Department.

Comments: On April 22, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up inspection of Oil and Gas Mgmt's Armstrong 2 gas well site located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County.This inspection is following IR 4160648, which documents violations that were issued for heavily rusted production equipment due to their corrosion posing the risk of a spill and/or release.This inspection is also following IR 4183514, which documents the Department attempted to contact the Operator to discuss various violations on site/on the access road, however, the phone number on the well tag was not in service, therefore violations were issued at that time for inaccurate information on the well tag. A Notice of Violation Operator response has yet to be received for the violations issued during IR 4160648, and site conditions appear to be unchanged.The Department's assessment of the shared portion of this access road as well as the direct portion of this access road can be found in IR 4186406 and IR 4186412.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the Armstrong 2 well site to be overgrown with vegetation, the Department recommends the Operator maintain the vegetation within the well site to ensure the well site remains accessible. A well tag was observed to be fixed to a heavily rusted gas well that did not appear to have updated Operator information posted on it. Violations issued for an inaccurate well tag are being continued at this time.At the time of this inspection, a heavily rusted production tank was also observed on site and connected for production, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this tank or gas wellhead at this time. The Department recommends the Operator monitor and maintain the structural integrity of the production tank and gas wellhead to ensure that corrosion does not worsen resulting in a release. Although no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed, a strong gas odor and hissing was still observed to be coming from the lower portion of the gas wellhead. Based on today's inspection, violations issues for heavily rusted production equipment posing the risk for a spill/release and for inaccurate operator information on the well tag/posting is to remain outstanding at this time.

Comments: There was a crude oil release from inside a tank battery located next to this well that occurred during the night on October 19th or early in the morning on the 20th. With more rain in the forecast Mr. Branch indicated they would be addressing any stray crude that may still be present in the coming days. The release looked largely remediated upon my arrival. The need for any additional cleanup measures will be evaluated during future inspection of this lease.

Comments: On 10/21/2021, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an incident inspection at the Greenzweig (U Pad). This inspection is to evaluate the site after an engine oil spill was reported to the department on 10/20/2021. When I arrived on site I met two SWN personnel, Mike Deming and Seth Tratthen. Also on site were two men from Resource Environmental Management Inc. I have contact info for John Salinkas. Description of event: A compressor station is in the process of being removed from the site. A crew from a third party company, Pilot Thomas, was removing fluids from the equipment prior to the equipment being loaded on trucks. Unused engine oil was being transferred from a 500-gallon tank to a 300-gallon tote that was already on a truck. The tote did not have a cap on the two inch drain valve and the tote was strapped down on the truck with the drain valve not immediately accessible by the crew. As the crew was pumping into the tote, they suspected something was wrong with the pumping process. They checked the progress and found the drain valve partially open and leaking fluids onto the ground. They stopped pumping and had to unstrap the tote before manhandling it to a position where they could reach and close the valve. It is estimated that 120 gallons of HDAX 5200 Low Ash Gas Engine OIl was released onto the unprotected ground. This was next to edge of the pad. A perimeter berm kept the fluid from flowing off property and down the fill slope. Response: A truck on site that could pick up fluids was used to collect 90 gallons of free liquid. A skid-steer was brought to location and excavated a 40' long x10' wide x2.5' (maximum measurements) trench. The excavated material was loaded into two 30yd rolloff dumpsters. While I was still on site, both dumpsters were loaded onto trucks and hauled away to an industrial landfill. I was shown the excavated area where the spill had impacted. I did not witness any signs of free liquid or additional contamination. I was told that the cleanup crew tested the excavation area to determine if clear of contamination before ending excavation. No E&S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. The site appears stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. There are a total of 3 wells staged for production. All wells are tagged with API/well permit numbers. The well cellars are filled with gravel. All GPUs and production tanks were stationed in secondary containment. This spill constitutes violations of these three regulations 78a 56(a), SWMA 301, and CSL 402(b) The department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation in accordance with 78a 66(c).

Comments: Routine site inspection at conventional well 033-25207 on May 02, 2025. Earth disturbance actives were observed around the production equipment. No E and S issues were observed. The well appears active and capable of producing. Flakey paint and corrosion was observed on the production equipment and axillary pipes. The Department recommends monitoring the equipment and repainting or replacing the equipment if needed. A 5x Altair gas meter was used to screen around the production equipment. No combustible or methane gases were detected.Please note during the inspection I observed a small drip coming from the release valve on the brine tank. I screened for conductivity all around the edge of the brine tank, readings ranged from 1.46 mS/cm to > 4.00 mS /cm. Please note, the Hanna soil probes max range is 4.00 mS/cm. Elevated readings range ~1-2ft. away from the brine tank. While onsite I notified Will Warfel and Heather Empfield of Diversified Production LLC. According to the lease operator, the fluids were last measured on April 2, 2025. The lease operator remeasured the fluids after I reported the leak. The measurement is ~1/2 inch lower than last month's fluids level within the tank. Therefore, they estimated ~10-15 gallons of fluids were released. The leak on the release valve was later fixed by the lease operator. Clean-up will take place during the week of May 5, 2025.Violations have been cited for the brine release.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ARMAC RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/22/2023
Violation Code: 78.91(a) - PLUGGING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Upon abandoning a well, the owner or operator failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore under 25 Pa. Code §§ 78.92—78.98 or an approved alternate method.
Violation ID: 999934
Permit API: 123-45286
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Warren City
Inspection Type: Compliance Evaluation
Inspection Date: 6/26/2023
Comments: This well was inspected as part of an active stray gas migration case (CTS# 369563). Previously this well was found to have methane detected outside of the well bore and the operator decided to plug the well. Upon completion of their plugging attempt they inadvertently cemented some of their tubing into the well. Subsequently a camera was ran into the well and bubbles were visibly seen at the top of fluid level. A MSA Altair 5X gas meter was used and determined the bubbles were methane being emitted into the well bore. A violation was issued to the operator for not properly plugging the well. To address this violation the operator is having a rig drill down to approx 550', which is 50' below the surface casing shoe and remove the cemented in tubing at which point another camera run will take place to see if the well is still bubbling methane. Today's operations: Bull Run Rig 118 drilled from 355.88' to 360.88' before getting rained out

properties.content:

Permit API: 129-23976
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Hempfield Township
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 9/10/2025
Comments: This Admin inspection is to document the receipt of a Well Site Restoration Report the Department received via email on 9/10/2025 from SK Operating Inc's Valerie Gressang for the Louis Yemc 1 plugged well site located in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 12/08/2023, therefore the site should have been restored no later than 9/08/2024. However, the site was not fully restored until 6/26/2025 (documented in IR 4016258). Pursuant to 78.65(3), the Operator shall submit a well site restoration report within 60 days of the restoration of the well site. Therefore, a well site restoration report should have been submitted to the Department on or before 8/25/2025. Prior to today's well site restoration report submission, a well site restoration report had not been received, therefore on 9/5/2025, violations were issued (documented in IR 4048190) for failure to submit a well site restoration report within 60 days of restoration.Based on the received Well Site Restoration Report, the Department is administratively denying the Well Site Restoration Report submission as Section G. "Site Restoration" is incomplete. Violations issued for failure to submit a Well Site Restoration Report within 60 days of the restoration of the well site shall remain outstanding at this time.
